chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who purchased a mature bondwoman who did not menstruate while with him until six months had passed for her, and there was no pregnancy.
He عليه السلام said: "If someone like her normally menstruates, and that is not due to old age, then this is a defect for which she may be returned."

key_terms.تَحِيضُ: she menstruates; indicating normal menstrual function
key_terms.تُرَدُّ: she is returned; meaning the sale may be rescinded on account of the defect
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a female bondwoman who is the subject of the sale
key_terms.حَبَلٌ: pregnancy, which would explain the absence of menstruation
key_terms.عَيْبٌ: a defect in the sold property that affects the purchaser's right
key_terms.كِبَرٍ: old age, a natural cause for cessation of menstruation
key_terms.مُدْرِكَةً: mature; having reached an age where menstruation is expected

ai.seo_question: When is the absence of menstruation considered a legal defect in the purchase of a bondwoman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a sale involving a bondwoman whose menstruation ceased for six months without pregnancy. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام states that if women like her normally menstruate and the cessation is not due to old age, then this is considered a defect that justifies returning her in the sale.
